links.outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with vs without visual annotation on X-ray advice
links.effect: Annotated advice raised accuracy overall (OR 2.30, p=0.002); IM/EM physicians improved by 5.66% (p=0.042); radiologists 3.41% (p=0.120, non-significant).
links.quote: When looking at the results separated by task expertise (defined by discipline), we found that providing annotated advice improved the mean performance of the IM/EM physicians in our experiment by 5.66% ( p = 0.042, see Fig. 2 a).

links.outcome: Effect of visual explanation of AI advice on diagnostic accuracy and advice quality rating
links.effect: Annotated (explainable) advice increased accuracy (OR 2.30, p=0.002) and quality ratings (+0.25, p=0.001); benefit significant for non-task experts, not for radiologists.
links.quote: The results indicate that having an explanation (i.e., annotation on the X-ray indicating the area that determined the prediction) as part of the advice positively affected physicians' diagnostic accuracy and their quality rating.

links.effect: Annotated advice: odds ratio 2.30, 95% CI 1.37–3.85, p = 0.002.

links.effect: Annotated advice quality estimate 0.25, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.39, p = 0.001.
links.quote: Participants rated the quality of the advice higher, on average, if it was given with an explanation, i.e., with a visible annotation on the X-ray.
